First, recall the associative law

$$
ABC=(AB)C=A(BC).
$$

Notice that $A$ is a $1\times 2$ matrix, $B$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix, and $C$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix. Therefore, 

- multiplying $A$ by $B$, we will obtain a $1\times 2$ matrix, which will require finding $2$ entries, while

- multiplying $B$ by $C$, we will obtain a $2\times 2$ matrix, which will require finding $4$ entries.

So, we find the product $AB$ first: 

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 6\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}10 & 34\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we multiply $AB$ by $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}ABC & =(AB)C \\  & =[\begin{aligned}10 & 34\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-58 & 136\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
